candidates.name: INSPIRE Index Polygons dataset
verified_facts: INSPIRE polygons show position and indicative extent of registered freehold property.
A title can contain several polygons and each polygon has its own Land Registry-INSPIRE ID.
The extent of land in a registered title cannot be established from INSPIRE polygons alone and requires the title plan.
semantic_limits: INSPIRE geometry is not promoted to an exact legal boundary.

candidates.name: INSPIRE July 2026 download
verified_facts: The current file set was published 5 July 2026.
Files are published on the first Sunday of each month.
Downloads are partitioned by local authority.
semantic_limits: Publication freshness does not establish exact geometry or terrain accuracy.

candidates.name: INSPIRE GML technical guidance
verified_facts: HMLR polygon data is captured against British National Grid.
The guidance identifies EPSG:27700 as the native measurement CRS.
It warns that conversion from BNG to WGS84 may shift some features by up to 15 metres.
semantic_limits: Reprojected web-map geometry is display evidence only for exact parcel sampling.

candidates.name: INSPIRE Index Polygons metadata
verified_facts: Metadata was last updated 8 July 2026.
The dataset is published by HM Land Registry under the Open Government Licence.
Download, information and view services are separately identified.
semantic_limits: Metadata and view services are not substitutes for exact source-file geometry.

candidates.name: National Polygon Service
verified_facts: The National Polygon Service includes National Polygon, Title Descriptor, and Title Number/UPRN datasets.
Every freehold or leasehold title has at least one index polygon.
The dataset is updated on the second working day of each month with previous-month data.
semantic_limits: NPS is licensed bulk data and is not silently substituted for the open INSPIRE source used by this slot.

candidates.name: National Polygon technical specification
verified_facts: The specification states that gaps, overlaps, slivers and underlaps exist in the polygon dataset.
Some technical overlaps arise from mapping inconsistencies and do not represent real title conflicts.
Actual overlaps can also occur and may be resolved through registration activity.
semantic_limits: Polygon topology anomalies must fail closed rather than be converted into terrain or ownership conclusions.

candidates.name: Title Number and UPRN Look Up technical specification
verified_facts: The dataset links title numbers to UPRNs only where an address relationship can be made.
Duplicate or unmatched addresses can exist.
The title number is the join identifier to other HMLR data.
semantic_limits: Address/UPRN linkage is not parcel geometry evidence and cannot replace the exact INSPIRE ID chain.

candidates.name: Title Descriptor technical specification
verified_facts: The dataset records estate interest and class of title.
Title class depends on the evidence lodged at registration.
Public-data quality is not guaranteed error-free or fit for every purpose.
semantic_limits: Tenure and title class do not establish parcel elevation or boundary coordinates.

candidates.name: MapSearch guidance
verified_facts: MapSearch can show whether land is registered and provide title numbers and tenure details.
Snapshot PDFs are stated to be for reference purposes only.
MapSearch does not provide the indemnity provisions of an official index-map search.
semantic_limits: MapSearch display output is not exact legal-boundary or terrain-sampling evidence.

candidates.name: Search the index map
verified_facts: The index map contains information on land and property registered or being registered with HMLR.
It can find title numbers where register-search results are insufficient.
The search can confirm that land is unregistered.
semantic_limits: Index-map search results identify registration records and do not supply terrain elevations.

candidates.name: Portal request a search of the index map
verified_facts: A plan is required where a verbal description does not precisely identify the search area.
An unsuitable plan can cause rejection of the application.
MapSearch and official index-map search are separate services.
semantic_limits: Plan acceptability for a registry search does not certify exact parcel geometry.

candidates.name: Alter title plan by removing land collection PG77
verified_facts: PG77 was last updated 1 June 2026.
It covers applications to alter a title plan by removing land.
Alteration requires a formal registration process rather than inference from map display.
semantic_limits: A suspected geometry mismatch is not treated as automatically corrected in source data.

candidates.name: Practice guide 77 detailed alteration guidance
verified_facts: The general-boundaries rule means red edging does not fix the precise legal boundary.
Land can be inside red edging yet outside the registered title, or vice versa, within the scope of the general-boundaries rule.
Applications for alteration require evidence.
semantic_limits: Title-plan edging is not converted into centimetric parcel geometry.

candidates.name: Practice guide 83 alteration
verified_facts: An application for alteration must clearly specify the alteration sought.
Evidence must accompany an alteration application.
The guidance separately references title-plan alteration under PG77.
semantic_limits: Potential source inconsistencies are logged as evidence issues rather than silently edited.

candidates.name: Notices and restrictions PG19 collection
verified_facts: PG19 was last updated 8 June 2026.
It concerns notices and restrictions protecting third-party interests in registered estates.
semantic_limits: Register interests are legal metadata and are not terrain-source observations.

candidates.name: Practice guide 19 detailed guidance
verified_facts: Where an interest affects only part of a registered title a plan should be included unless the part is already clearly identified on the title plan.
Notices and restrictions have different registration effects.
semantic_limits: A part-title interest plan is not used as the canonical polygon for terrain sampling.

candidates.name: Practice guide 40 plans overview
verified_facts: PG40 separates basis-of-plans, preparing-plans, boundaries, determined-boundaries, title-plan and plan-service guidance into distinct supplements.
The overview explicitly separates these different evidence roles.
semantic_limits: No single plan-guide category is treated as proof of terrain height.

candidates.name: OS MasterMap Topography Layer documentation
verified_facts: OS defines absolute accuracy, relative accuracy and geometric fidelity separately.
Absolute accuracy compares dataset coordinates with ground coordinates in British National Grid.
semantic_limits: Topographic horizontal accuracy is kept separate from EA vertical LiDAR RMSE.

candidates.name: OS NGD capture specification values
verified_facts: OS NGD capture specification labels expected base-survey positional accuracy by area.
Published minimum RMSE values include 0.5m urban, 1.1m rural and 4.1m moorland.
semantic_limits: These are horizontal base-map capture classes and do not reduce terrain-source uncertainty.

candidates.name: OS NGD Field Boundary known limitations
verified_facts: Closely spaced parallel features can be generalized and one feature selected over another.
Woodland and moorland conditions can reduce classification reliability.
The page identifies known areas where data quality may be lower.
semantic_limits: OS field-boundary classification is never treated as a cadastral legal boundary.

candidates.name: OS MasterMap Terrain and Height
verified_facts: Topography Layer contains selected known-height point features rather than terrain contours.
Spot heights are shown to one decimal metre.
OS states historic benchmark information cannot be guaranteed accurate.
semantic_limits: Spot heights and historic benchmarks are diagnostic only and do not replace the EA DTM polygon sample.

candidates.name: OS MasterMap Imagery Layer image appearance
verified_facts: Imagery absolute accuracy is expressed as horizontal RMSE in National Grid.
The page states an absolute imagery accuracy of 1.1m RMSE.
Mosaicing and edge matching can join imagery captured at different times.
semantic_limits: Orthophoto alignment is visual/horizontal evidence and is not a terrain elevation source.

candidates.name: OS NGD positional accuracy value
verified_facts: OS NGD publishes explicit positional-accuracy categories for address coordinates.
The code list includes low-accuracy and internal-position categories.
semantic_limits: Address-coordinate quality categories are not parcel-boundary or terrain accuracy measures.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 50 per-tile metadata
verified_facts: Metadata records British National Grid and ODN references.
Flying dates are separated from tile processing date.
Version, change reason and lineage are separately recorded.
semantic_limits: Terrain 50 is coarse sanity evidence and its processing date is not treated as acquisition date.

candidates.name: LIDAR Vegetation Object Model
verified_facts: The VOM is derived from National LIDAR Programme 1m elevation data plus OS mapping and Sentinel-2 imagery.
It represents vegetation canopy height above ground.
The product is fully automated and states that no manual QC/editing is applied beyond visual checks.
semantic_limits: Derived canopy/object height products are excluded from primary bare-earth parcel measurement.

candidates.name: OGC API Environmental Data Retrieval 1.1 standard
verified_facts: EDR defines Position, Radius, Area, Cube, Trajectory and Corridor query patterns.
Area queries require explicit coordinate geometry and can carry CRS, parameter and time controls.
Position matching behavior can depend on the collection implementation.
semantic_limits: EDR query conformance does not prove numeric equivalence to the canonical EA WCS sample.

candidates.name: OGC API Common Part 1 Core
verified_facts: OGC API Common defines shared HTTP, URI, landing-page and conformance building blocks.
Conformance declarations advertise implemented requirements classes.
semantic_limits: API conformance declarations are capability metadata and do not validate elevation values.

candidates.name: OGC API Features Part 2 CRS by Reference
verified_facts: The standard defines discovery of supported CRSs and use of crs and bbox-crs parameters.
Unsupported CRS requests require an error response.
If no CRS is requested the Part 1 default CRS applies.
semantic_limits: Feature geometry CRS negotiation is explicit and cannot silently substitute display CRS for EPSG:27700 measurement geometry.

candidates.name: OGC API Features Part 3 Filtering
verified_facts: Part 3 defines CQL2 filtering and queryables.
Filter predicates are combined with other filtering parameters using logical AND.
When CRS filtering is implemented the filter-crs parameter is validated against supported CRS identifiers.
semantic_limits: A filtered feature response still requires source identity and CRS validation before geometry use.

candidates.name: OGC API Tiles Part 1 Core
verified_facts: Tiles Part 1 defines core tile-access requirements.
Implementations advertise supported conformance classes.
Tile API conformance can be combined with OGC API Common.
semantic_limits: Tile conformance and indexing do not establish that tile content is numeric elevation.

candidates.name: CoverageJSON Community Standard
verified_facts: CoverageJSON explicitly separates domain, range and coverage objects.
Domain objects contain axes and referencing information.
Range encodings include NdArray and TiledNdArray structures.
semantic_limits: Representation structure does not prove source elevation accuracy.

candidates.name: GeoPackage Encoding Standard 1.3
verified_facts: A GeoPackage must include a spatial reference system table.
All SRS values used by GeoPackage contents must be defined.
Feature and tile contents reference SRS definitions through standard schema relationships.
semantic_limits: GeoPackage container/SRS conformance does not turn metadata indexes into terrain values.

candidates.name: OGC API Features Part 1 Core
verified_facts: Part 1 defines feature collection access and core filtering behavior.
It includes support for GML Simple Features Profile Level 0 as a feature encoding.
The GML profile is limited to two-dimensional linear or planar geometries.
semantic_limits: Feature encoding support is not cadastral or elevation accuracy evidence.
